headline_result: **Of the 35 batches `01-manifest.json` lists as not yet built by batch number, 18 were already built or correctly resolved under different, uncross-referenced tracking — cutting the genuine remaining backlog from "46/47 remain" (the planning doc's stale figure) to 16 batches that actually need research.** The FIGARO/GFS/monetary-aggregates/CBD2 stack (batches 47–62, minus the known-duplicate 54) and the ECB/Eurosystem collateral-and-balance-sheet stack (batches 68–72) — both of which `planning/MISSION-TODO-2.md` item 5 explicitly named as "also unbuilt and coherent" and "the project's largest known backlog by volume" — turned out to be **entirely already covered**, batch 47/51/52/53/55/56/61/62 and 68 built as real nodes (`eurostat-edp-gfs-ecb-statistics.json`, `eurosystem-ecb.json`), batches 48/49/50/60/65 built via a separate docx backlog pass (`eu-meta-docx-batches.json`), and batches 69–72 correctly read and dropped (operational collateral law, not a recurring titled report) rather than left unread. Batch 63 (MIP auxiliary indicators) is genuinely half-open — read, partly minted (the quality report), partly dropped pending an edge decision — not untouched. Batch 38 is 4/6 redundant with an already-built document, with a small (2-record) genuinely new remainder about the post-2027 European Statistical Programme. What is left, confirmed by this session's grep pass to have **zero** existing corpus coverage, is the fourteen-batch ESA-2010-methodology stack (batches 0, 1, 2, 5–15 — Annex A/B legal text, CPA/NACE Regulation 451/2008, the quarterly-financial-accounts-for-general-government manual, the 2022 Manual on Government Deficit and Debt, the 2026 Statistical Requirements Compendium, the SUT/IOT and QNA handbooks), plus batch 46 (unchanged: 29 uncitable peer-review records, still last), plus batch 38's small remainder.

findings.heading: 1. The FIGARO/GFS/monetary-aggregates/CBD2 stack (batches 47–62) is entirely already built, under two separate untracked efforts
findings.body: `eurostat-edp-gfs-ecb-statistics.json`'s own `_status` field states plainly: "Verified from staged batches in `EU/slices/_staging/10-batch-with-records.ndjson` (indices 47, 51, 52, 53, 54, 55, 56, 61, 62)" — a "Priority C" pass dated 2026-08-05, per `G.41.md`/`G.42.md`. Separately, `eu-meta-docx-batches.json`'s `_note` states it worked "Seven distinct staged batches inside the docx (SUT-IOT, FIGARO, GLOBAL-IO, PEER-REVIEWS-3RD-ROUND, REC-2023-397, ESGAB-ANNUAL-REPORTS, WP-SMP-ESAC)... never copied into the staging ndjson pipeline that fed prior sessions' work" — also dated 2026-08-05. Matching those batch_ids against `01-manifest.json`: SUT-IOT is batch 48 (→ `eurostat-suiot`), FIGARO is batch 49 (→ `eurostat-figaro`), GLOBAL-IO is batch 50 (→ `oecd-icio`, with WIOD/EXIOBASE/EORA/GTAP-MRIO/OECD-TiVA correctly filed as `no-document` leads, not silently dropped), WP-SMP-ESAC is batch 60 (→ `eurostat-annual-work-programme` + `esac-opinion-work-programme`). Both efforts predate item 5's own batch-number tracking (started `G.50.md`, 2026-08-07) by two days, and neither cross-referenced the other or item 5's own prose. Batches 57, 58, 59 in this same numeric range were already credited via `G.69.md`'s cluster. That leaves only batches 54 (byte-identical duplicate of 53, per the manifest's own hand-added note) genuinely accounted for as "not separately built" rather than "built" — every other number in 47–62 now has a real node or a real, reasoned drop behind it.

findings.heading: 2. Batch 65 is the same document as `eurostat-annual-work-programme`, not a second one
findings.body: Batch 65's scope reads "2026 Work Programme under Single Market Programme – Annex IV to C(2025) 8895: legal basis, budget breakdown, objectives" with record IDs `smp-wp-2026-intro-legal`, `smp-wp-2026-budget`, `smp-wp-2026-capacity-domains`. `eurostat-annual-work-programme`'s own description (built from batch 60, per Finding 1) says: "Annex IV to the Commission's annual financing decision for the Single Market Programme... The 2026 edition's own text: 'The 2026 WP will be the sixth one implementing the Single Market Programme 2021-2027.'" Same instrument, same Annex IV, same C(2025) 8895 financing decision — batch 65 is a second staged fragment of a document batch 60 already fully covered, not new material. No new work needed; confirmed rather than built.

findings.heading: 3. The ECB/Eurosystem collateral stack (batches 68–72) was fully read and correctly resolved, not skipped
findings.body: `eurostat-edp-gfs-ecb-statistics.json` carries a `_dropped` entry titled "Eurosystem collateral framework: margin calls, valuation haircuts, fixed-term deposits" describing "Four fully-read staged batches (Guideline (EU) 2015/510 and its amendments -- margin calls, the 2026 haircut amendment, NCB implementation duty, fixed-term deposits)... describe operational law governing collateral management, not a recurrently published titled report. Fails the node test on the same grounds as EBS Regulation 2019/2152." Checked against the manifest directly: batch 69's `record_ids` (`guid-2015-510-def-margin-call`, `guid-2015-510-art128-variation-margins`...) are margin calls; batch 70's (`guid-2026-690-title`, `guid-2026-690-table-2a`...) are the 2026 haircut amendment; batch 71's (`guid-2016-65-art6-ncb-implementation`...) are NCB implementation duty; batch 72's (`guid-2015-510-def-fixed-term-deposits`...) are fixed-term deposits. Exact match to the dropped entry's own description, batch for batch. Batch 68 (Guideline (EU) 2024/2941, the consolidated-balance-sheet legal framework) is separately covered: `eurosystem-ecb.json`'s `_note` states two of its three reports "verify and promote a previously-staged batch (`EU/slices/_staging/10-batch-with-records.ndjson`, index 68)" — `ecb-eurosystem-annual-balance-sheet` and `ecb-eurosystem-weekly-financial-statement`. This whole five-batch block, which `planning/MISSION-TODO-2.md` item 5(b) named as "also unbuilt" material belonging to "priority C's own material," turns out to have been priority C's own material in the fullest sense — already read and closed by priority C itself.

findings.heading: 4. Batch 63 (MIP) is half-open, not untouched, and the open half has a clear next step already written down
findings.body: Batch 63's `record_ids` are `mip-aux-2026-list-intro`, `mip-aux-2026-full-list`, `mip-quality-3level-framework`, `mip-sources-main`, `mip-ess-escb-quality-report-2026`, `mip-gfs-edp-debt-link`. One of these — `mip-ess-escb-quality-report-2026` — is already a real node: `eurosystem-ecb.json` carries `ess-escb-mip-quality-report` ("ESS-ESCB Quality Assessment Report on Statistics Underlying the Macroeconomic Imbalance Procedure"). The rest of the batch (the MIP auxiliary-indicator list and its 3-level quality framework, plus the MIP scoreboard/Alert Mechanism Report itself) is the subject of a `_dropped` entry in `eurostat-edp-gfs-ecb-statistics.json` re-touched twice already: originally dropped 2026-08-05 as `no-document` (cadence not demonstrated), then re-checked live 2026-08-09 during the corpus-wide sweep and found to have clean cadence evidence ("a document issued by the European Commission towards the end of the calendar year... dated editions listed back to 2012") — but still not minted, because, in that entry's own words, "no document read by this session's predecessor or this session names it as an input to, or output of, anything else in this file's material." This is a genuine open item, but a narrow one: the cadence work is done, and what's missing is one search for what edge, if any, the AMR/MIP scoreboard belongs on. Flagged forward as a cheap check (see below), not folded into the "16 batches remain" count, since it is not unread material.

findings.heading: 5. Batch 38 splits cleanly into an already-covered half and a small new half
findings.body: Batch 38's six `record_ids` split by subject: `wp2026-legal-basis`, `wp2026-objectives`, `wp2026-focus-areas`, `wp2026-thematic-priorities` name the same 2026 Work Programme document already built as `eurostat-annual-work-programme` (per Finding 1/2 — legal basis, objectives and focus areas are simply more fragments of the same Annex IV document batches 60 and 65 already cover from other angles). The other two — `ess-common-position-esp-link` and `esac-post2027-priorities` — are about a different, forward-looking document: the batch's own scope names it as "Link from ESS common position (May 2025) to the preparation of the next European Statistical Programme under post-2027 MFF" and "ESAC opinion on draft programming framework for European statistics post-2027 (August 2025)." Grepped for "post-2027," "European Statistical Programme," and "common position" across the full corpus — zero hits. This is genuinely new, but it is two records, not a six-record batch; whoever next works item 5 should treat batch 38 as effectively already 2/3 done and pick up only its post-2027 remainder.

corrections.text: `planning/MISSION-TODO-2.md` item 5, "26 of 73 batches built, 47 remain" and the (b)/"also unbuilt and coherent" text (originally `G.50.md`-era, 2026-08-07) — overstated the remaining backlog by roughly 3x.** Not wrong about what those sessions had themselves built (the count was accurate for work done *under item 5's own tracking*), but wrong to describe batches 47–62 minus the known cluster, 65, and 68–72 as unbuilt or uncharacterised material, when two earlier and separately-tracked sessions (`G.41.md`/`G.42.md`'s Priority C pass, and the `EU Meta jsons.docx` backlog pass, both 2026-08-05) had already built or correctly resolved nearly all of it. This is not a case of anyone doing the work wrong — both covering files are well-evidenced and internally consistent — it is a tracking gap: item 5's own prose was never cross-checked against the rest of the corpus before being written, the same class of bug `G.63.md`'s stale-cross-file finding and `[[cheap-check-grep-first]]` already named for individual node leads, now confirmed to apply at the batch-cluster level too (as `G.69.md` Finding 1 first suspected and this session confirms in full). Corrected in place this session, with a dated `**CORRECTION 2026-08-09**` block rather than an edit to the original prose, per `Research.1.md`'s never-edit-a-predecessor convention extended to planning documents (the same convention `G.69.md` itself followed for the scoping-doc archival).

session_conditions: A single-focus session on Thomas's (relayed) instruction to run the corpus-grep pass `G.69.md` itself recommended as the next step, rather than deep-reading the next batch cluster directly. No new staged records were read from `10-batch-with-records.ndjson` this session — the entire session was cross-referencing `01-manifest.json`'s batch metadata (`scope`/`batch_id`/`strand`/`record_ids`) against the existing corpus's own text, node IDs, and `_status`/`_note` fields, via `grep` and small Python scripts run through `device_bash`. No primary source was fetched or re-verified this session; every claim here rests on matching staged-batch record IDs and scope strings against what earlier sessions already wrote and cited, not on independent verification of those earlier sessions' citations. `npm run validate` was not run (no data file changed) and was not needed — this session touched exactly one file, a planning document, not `src/data/research/*.json` or `src/data/index.ts`.
